thesis.name: Permission to operate
thesis.coreBelief: The next durable AI companies sell into markets where the bottleneck is permission, not the model. In regulated industries that permission is certification, liability and a buyer's trust; in physical AI it is the safety case, procurement and real-world data that cannot be scraped. The moats are the same in both: compliance work competitors must repeat, proprietary operating data, and slow buyers whose switching costs run for a decade. Both have to pass through the same layer that grants the permission: evaluation, security, simulation and certification. And before any of it, the models have to be taught the work by the people who already hold the permission.

sectors.name: Regulated vertical AI
sectors.description: AI built for licensed professions and regulated workflows: health, legal, tax and accounting, financial services, veterinary and dental.

sectors.name: Defence and dual-use
sectors.description: Command and control, ISR, electronic warfare, uncrewed systems and critical-infrastructure protection, sold to ministries and primes.

sectors.name: Robotics and autonomy
sectors.description: Robot learning, humanoids, autonomous vehicles and vessels, and software-run factories reshoring critical manufacturing.

sectors.name: AI assurance
sectors.description: The permission layer: evaluation, AI security, governance and compliance, simulation and certification that regulated and physical AI must pass through.

sectors.name: Training data and evals
sectors.description: Expert data, RL environments and evaluations that teach and test frontier models on professional work. The same doctors, lawyers and bankers whose sign-off grants the permission are now the ones teaching the models.

edition.note: A new fifth orbit, Training data and evals: the experts and environments that teach the models. Labelbox's Series E is this week's news.
